_meta.indication: ZERBAXA is indicated in patients 18 years or older for complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI, in combination with metronidazole) and complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by designated susceptible microorganisms

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CXA-cIAI-10-08&09 (pooled from CXA-cIAI-10-08 and CXA-cIAI-10-09), the Phase 3 cIAI trial
pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, double-blind trial comparing ZERBAXA plus metronidazole to meropenem for 4 to 14 days of therapy in adults hospitalized with cIAI
pivotal_trials.population: Adults hospitalized with complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical response (clinical cure), defined as complete resolution or significant improvement in signs and symptoms at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit, in the microbiological intent-to-treat (MITT) population
pivotal_trials.n: 979 randomized; MITT population 806 (389 ZERBAXA + metronidazole, 417 meropenem)
pivotal_trials.result: MITT clinical cure 83% (323/389) ZERBAXA + metronidazole vs 87.3% (364/417) meropenem; treatment difference -4.3 (95% CI -9.2, 0.7), meeting non-inferiority

nct_ctgov.title: Study Comparing the Safety and Efficacy of Intravenous CXA-201 and Intravenous Meropenem in Complicated Intraabdominal Infections

pivotal_trials.trial_name: The Phase 3 cUTI trial pooled from CXA-cUTI-10-04 and CXA-cUTI-10-05
pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, double-blind trial comparing ZERBAXA to levofloxacin (750 mg IV once daily) for 7 days in adults hospitalized with cUTI including pyelonephritis
pivotal_trials.population: Adults hospitalized with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of complete resolution/marked improvement of clinical symptoms plus microbiological eradication at the TOC visit in the microbiologically modified intent-to-treat (mMITT) population
pivotal_trials.result: mMITT composite cure 76.9% (306/398) ZERBAXA vs 68.4% (275/402) levofloxacin; treatment difference 8.5 (95% CI 2.3, 14.6)

nct_ctgov.title: Study Comparing the Safety and Efficacy of Intravenous CXA-201 and Intravenous Levofloxacin in Complicated Urinary Tract Infection, Including Pyelonephritis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% in either indication) are nausea, diarrhea, headache, and pyrexia. In cIAI (N=482): nausea 7.9%, diarrhea 6.2%, pyrexia 5.6%; in cUTI (N=533): headache 5.8%. Serious risks include hypersensitivity reactions and Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea.
target_moa: Ceftolozane is a cephalosporin whose bactericidal action results from inhibition of cell wall biosynthesis via binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits certain beta-lactamases
modality: Small molecule: fixed combination of a cephalosporin antibacterial (ceftolozane sulfate) and a beta-lactamase inhibitor (tazobactam sodium)

advisory_committee.vote: This NDA was not discussed by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication, for the treatment of Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and Ventilator-Associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP).

description.text: Added pediatric patients from birth to less than 18 years to the approved indication for complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for the addition of pediatric patients from birth to less than 18 years of age to the approved indications for treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis (S-011), and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) (S-012).

description.text: Expanded HABP/VABP indication to include pediatric patients (at least 32 weeks gestational age)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for expansion of the approved indication for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP) to include pediatric patients (at least 32 weeks gestational age). Additionally, the age range for the pediatric patients for the approved indications of complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI), where Zerbaxa is used in combination with metronidazole, and complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, was updated to read as “at least 32 weeks gestational age” instead of “birth to less than 18 years old.”

basis.text: Granted fast track designation for the cIAI and cUTI indications on February 20, 2013, and May 7, 2013, respectively

citations.quote: Ceftolozane-tazobactam was granted qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) designation for the cIAI and cUTI indications on December 5, 2012, and February 20, 2013, respectively, and fast track designation on February 20, 2013, and May 7, 2013, respectively.

basis.text: As ceftolozane-tazobactam has QIDP designation, it received a priority review under GAIN/FDASIA

citations.quote: As ceftolozane-tazobactam has QIDP designation, it received a priority review.

basis.text: Granted qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) designation for the cIAI and cUTI indications on December 5, 2012, and February 20, 2013, respectively

citations.quote: Ceftolozane-tazobactam was granted qualified infectious disease product (QIDP) designation for the cIAI and cUTI indications on December 5, 2012, and February 20, 2013, respectively, and fast track designation on February 20, 2013, and May 7, 2013, respectively.

summary.text: This 505(b)(2) NDA (relying on the Agency's previous finding of safety of tazobactam) was granted QIDP designation and fast track, and received a priority review under GAIN; it was not discussed by an advisory committee and was approved for cIAI (with metronidazole) and cUTI.

citations.quote: This application is covered under Section 505(b)(2) of the Food Drug and Cosmetic Act as the Applicant is relying on the Agency’s previous finding of safety of tazobactam, one of the components of the drug product, ceftolozane-tazobactam.
As ceftolozane-tazobactam has QIDP designation, it received a priority review.
This NDA was not discussed by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee.

requirement.text: Required pediatric study (2809-1): randomized, double-blind, multicenter comparative study of safety and tolerability of ceftolozane/tazobactam vs meropenem in hospitalized children from birth to <18 years with cUTI

citations.quote: 2809-1 Conduct a randomized, double blind, multicenter, comparative study to establish the safety and tolerability profile of cefzolozane/tazobactam compared to that of meropenem in hospitalized children from birth to <18 years with cUTI.

requirement.text: Required pediatric study (2809-2): randomized, double-blind, multicenter comparative study of safety and tolerability of ceftolozane/tazobactam vs meropenem in hospitalized children from birth to <18 years with cIAI

citations.quote: 2809-2 A randomized, double blind, multicenter, comparative study to establish the safety and tolerability profile of cefzolozane/tazobactam compared to that of meropenem in hospitalized children from birth to <18 years with cIAI.

requirement.text: Required study (2809-3) under 505(o): prospective five-year study after market introduction to determine if decreased susceptibility to ZERBAXA is occurring in the target bacterial population in the approved label

citations.quote: 2809-3 Conduct a prospective study over a five-year period after the introduction of ZERBAXA (cefotolozane/tazobactam) to the market to determine if decreased susceptibility to ZERBAXA (cefotolozane/tazobactam) is occurring in the target population of bacteria that are in the approved ZERBAXA (cefotolozane/tazobactam) label.
